chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kumundani, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Sadqa, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'Some of our companions have narrated that it is permissible for a man to marry his son's slave girl and his daughter's slave girl. I have a daughter and a son, and for my daughter I bought a slave girl from her dowry. Is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her?' He said: 'No, except with her permission.'
Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said: 'Is it not that this has come as permissible?' He said: 'Yes, that is if he himself is the cause (of acquiring her).'

Then he turned to me and gestured towards me with his index finger and said: 'When you buy for your daughter a slave girl or for your son, and the son is young and has not had intercourse with her, it is permissible for you to take possession of her and marry her. Otherwise, it is not permissible except with the permission of both of them.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father marry his young son's slave girl if he bought her from the daughter's dowry?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal ruling regarding a father's right to marry his young son's slave girl, which he acquired from the daughter's dowry. The Imam distinguishes between the father's direct acquisition and the son's ownership, ruling that if the son is young and has not consummated the marriage with the slave girl, the father may take possession and marry her; otherwise, the permission of both the son and the slave girl is required.
